content.text: The tainted header name (`param`/`bar`) flows unsanitized (just base64 encode/decode roundtrip, no validation) into `fileName` which is used in `open()` for writing — a classic path traversal sink. No sanitization breaks the taint.

input.justification:
User-controlled input (an arbitrary HTTP header name not in the common header name list) is assigned to `param`, then base64-encoded and decoded (a no-op transformation that does not sanitize or validate the value) into `bar`, which is concatenated into `fileName` and passed to `open(fileName, 'wb')`. There is no check that `bar`/`param` is restricted to a safe filename (no path traversal character filtering, no allowlist, no canonicalization/containment check against TESTFILES_DIR). An attacker can supply a header name containing `../` sequences to write to arbitrary file paths, demonstrating a genuine path injection vulnerability.</justification>
